findings.claim: Delivery specifies a single per-artifact SHA-256, published before any bytes move and auto-verified against on completion, while the same delivery step is specified elsewhere to rewrite the artifact's bytes per buyer (embedded tempo/key/loop metadata, and a per-buyer forensic watermark). Both cannot hold: for every content product the delivered bytes cannot match the published hash, so the specified verification fails and E-19's escalation path quarantines correctly-delivered builds.
findings.evidence: 14.03.01-download-delivery-resumable-transfer.md:73 '| Checksum | **SHA-256, published as copyable text** beside the download control | Auto-verified for the Musician; hand-verifiable for the air-gapped Operator (D-09). |' — :82 '3. System shows, **before any bytes move**: download size, **unpacked size** (D-02), version, SHA-256…' — :89 '10. On completion, SHA-256 is verified automatically against the published checksum.' — :114 (E-19) 'A second failure means the **stored artifact** is bad — every buyer of that build will hit it. Escalate: alert vendor and platform, quarantine the build from new grants.' — :184 (D-09) 'The SHA-256 is published as **copyable text**, so the Operator verifies by hand on a machine that has never met us.' CONTRADICTED BY 14.03.05-per-buyer-forensic-watermarking.md:32 'Marking makes each delivered artifact unique, which is why it collides head-on with edge caching (CX-04)…' and :39 '3. Delivery generates a buyer-unique mark and stamps it during transfer (CX-04).' AND BY 14.04.01-sample-loop-pack-catalog.md:275 (D-06) '**Delivered files carry embedded tempo/key/loop metadata**; an estimated key is embedded only where declaration and extraction agree' AND BY digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:35 (CX-24) 'Delivered audio must be **written** with embedded tempo/key/loop metadata (ACIDized-WAV / Apple-Loops), not merely served… This lands on the *same* delivery step as per-buyer watermarking: two writers on one artifact.'
findings.notFlagged: No marker on either side. The nearest tracked question, 14.04.01 Q-07, asks only 'which feature owns writing bytes at delivery?' and names caching as the consequence: 'Embedded metadata (D-06) and per-buyer watermarking (14.03.05) both modify the same file on the same delivery step, and 14.03.05 DT-02 already establishes that this step cannot be cached at the edge… Two writers on an uncacheable path is an architecture question with a product trigger' (14.04.01:293). It never reaches the published checksum. 14.03.01 Q-05 likewise enumerates only CDN, P2P and delta patching as the foreclosed defences.
findings.materiality: 14.03.01, 14.03.03 and 14.04.01 are all MUST-band (moscow-ledger.md:136-138); metadata embedding is not optional for the store's declared launch inventory. Watermarking (14.03.05) is COULD, so metadata embedding alone is enough to fire the contradiction.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the integrity contract: (a) publish the pre-write artifact hash and accept that every content download fails E-19 verification and quarantines the build; (b) compute a per-grant hash after the stamp, which cannot be shown 'before any bytes move' on a 100 GB streamed write and destroys D-09's hand-verification story; or (c) hash only the unwritten payload and invent a second, unspecified verification object. Nothing in the tree chooses.

findings.claim: The decline state is specified to offer, in words, a 14-day cancel-for-full-refund right, while the same file forbids naming a cancellation right to non-EU/UK buyers — and the locked launch market makes every launch buyer non-EU/UK, with the above-floor policy explicitly unset. The existence and the wording of the pre-delivery cancellation path at launch are therefore both undetermined.
findings.evidence: 14.09.01-withdrawal-right-waiver-capture.md:125 (E-01) User Sees: '"You can download once you accept that delivery starts immediately. Or cancel for a full refund within 14 days — or wait: from <date> this download will start without asking." The third option is stated, because concealing it would be the hostile version of an honest rule.' — :126 (E-02) 'A distinct, one-click "Cancel this order" path on the library row for 14 days' — :161 (States/Empty) 'a plain "Cancel for a full refund until <date>" beside it'. CONTRADICTED BY :144 (E-20) '**Buyer outside the EU/UK/EEA** | The gate still fires — no territorial branch (D-08) — but with neutral wording that does not assert a right they never had. Naming a 14-day right to a buyer who has none is a misrepresentation that could manufacture the very right it describes. | "By downloading now you agree delivery starts immediately." **No mention of a cancellation right.**' Launch audience per 14.09.01:232 (Q-04, RESOLVED): 'launch sales are US-first… every launch buyer meets the neutral wording D-08 already specifies for non-EU/UK'. Policy above the floor is open: :229 (Q-01) 'with a US-first launch there is no statutory floor to sit above, so the policy is not a top-up — it is the entire consumer position.' The same statutory framing is restated as unconditional behaviour in the sibling: 14.09.02-digital-refund-eligibility-adjudication.md:149 'Statutory backstop: this path must remain available for **14 days from purchase** (Art. 9(2)(a)) regardless of the store's discretionary policy' and :279 (D-06).
findings.materiality: 14.09.01 and 14.09.02 are both MUST-band and both ship in v1.5 (moscow-ledger.md:141-142). The gate's firing behaviour itself is unambiguous (D-08, D-15); what is contradictory is the cancellation entitlement the decline/empty states advertise.
findings.forcedInvention: For a US buyer who declines the waiver, an implementer must invent either (a) the promise, offering a one-click 14-day full refund with no policy decision behind it, or (b) the silence, leaving the Declined and Empty states with no stated exit and contradicting E-01's explicit 'the third option is stated' requirement and D-09's 'the decline message states the date the gate stops asking'.

coverageNote: Enumeration matches the expected 11 units / 64 files exactly. Depth is not uniform and the difference is disclosed: the corpus is 1,173,597 characters (~290K tokens), which cannot be ingested raw in one session. Read at full depth: the domain root index and CX in full, the whole 14.09 unit (index, CX, 14.09.01 in full; 14.09.02 and 14.09.03 with all sections except Role Lens / Deep Think / Cross-Cut Notes), 14.03.05 in full, 14.01.02 in full. Read section-selective for the remaining 54 files: every Decisions row and every Open Questions row (206 Q rows, 100% parsed), plus targeted full-text reads of Edge Case / Concrete-parameter / States rows surfaced by four whole-corpus programmatic sweeps (required-section presence on all 64 files; tracking-marker inventory on all 64; 206-sentence numeric-claim cross-comparison on all 64; checksum/integrity sweep on all 64). Skipped at prose level in those 54 files: Role Lens tables, Deep Think rationale narrative, and Cross-Cut Notes pointer lists — presence of each was verified programmatically, and the blocking finding F-01 was in fact recovered from a sweep rather than a linear read. Scoring denominators are small (5 applicable checkpoints for each sub-domain unit) because Constraint Explicitness, Success Measurability and Competitive Positioning are owned by meta/constraints.md, meta/ success metrics and meta/competitive-landscape.md respectively — none of which is in this domain's scope; the domain root retains Constraint Explicitness and Competitive Positioning because it authors both (cx:559-572 routing table; index:13 named-competitor differentiation). The small denominators inflate the percentage per finding: 10.5 points / 57 checkpoints = 18.42%, of which 9.0 points are ⚠️ half-marks and 1.0 is the single ❌. One structural caveat worth passing upstream: 23 of the tree's PENDING markers point at `/ideate-discover Step 5`, a stage this tree elsewhere treats as complete (every owner question in the domain index reads 'Deferral re-pointed from the completed /ideate-validate'), so those 23 cells are unreachable by any future stage — findings F-03 through F-11 and F-14 enumerate all of them by file and line.
